title: szokott → szokás volt: Customs of the Past

sections.title: Habitual Life and Border Warfare Routines
sections.content: You know *szokott* + infinitive and *gyakran* from A1 Unit 17, and adverbs in *-an/-en* such as *folyamatosan* from A2 Unit 19. History texts say what was customary in the past with *szokás volt* + infinitive: *Szokás volt portyázni* ('it was the custom to raid'). *rendszeresen* ('regularly') and *folyamatosan* ('continuously') say how often.

sections.title: How to say it was the custom
rows: It was the custom to raid.
Szokás volt a szürkemarhát nyugatra hajtani.
It was the custom to drive the grey cattle west.

items.spanish: A végvári vitézek rendszeresen portyáztak a határvidéken, hogy megvédjék a falvakat.
items.english: Border fortress warriors regularly raided the borderlands to protect the villages.

items.spanish: A két sereg bajnokai között szokás volt a bajvívás a várak falai előtt.
items.english: Between the champions of the two armies, it was customary to engage in single combat before the fortress walls.

items.spanish: A mezővárosok kereskedői évente több tízezer szürkemarhát hajtottak a nyugati piacokra.
items.english: Merchants from the market towns drove tens of thousands of grey cattle to the western markets every year.
